messages:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — Guppy Labs asked for a Q3 reserved capacity proposal. They need steady throughput + predictable burst support and want p99 latency aligned with their 99.5% SLA. Can we sync on sizing and safety margin?
Alex Patel: Quick q: do we have their token/sec or prompt mix? That drives GPU-hour estimate.
Maria Chen: They sent a spreadsheet earlier: baseline ~12M tokens/day, expected campaign multiplies to ~36M/day for 3 weeks. 80% of traffic is chat-gen, rest embeddings.
Jon Reynolds: Ok. Rough back-of-envelope: with our current runtime perf (chat gen ~0.9 tokens/sec per A10G-eq at typical seq lengths), baseline = ~154 GPU-hours/day; peak campaign ~462 GPU-hours/day. Monthly baseline ~4.6k GPU-hours, campaign adds ~1.3k for the burst period.
Tess Wu: Important for pricing: committed hourly rate is ~ $1.85/GPU-hour on a yearly reserve vs on-demand ~ $3.10. If they commit too low we eat burst premium.
Alex Patel: My read: target commit = baseline * 1.15 (safety band) => ~5.3k GPU-hours/month reserve. Keep 20% burst pool available (or on-demand fallback) for campaign peaks. That gives room for 36M/day spikes.
Jon Reynolds: Could also pursue a mixed strategy: smaller commit + guaranteed burst credits + autoscale policy with pre-warmed warm-pools. Operationally easier for us and lower sticker.
capacity-bot: Simulation run summary:
```
scenario: baseline + 3-week campaign
steady_reserve: 5.3k GPU-hours/mo
projected_burst_on_demand: 1.4k GPU-hours (campaign window)
utilization_est: steady 65% of reserve, peak 120% -> requires burst
estimated_extra_cost: $4.3k on-demand premium/month
```
Maria Chen: Two policy questions: 1) minimum safety margin (we suggested 15% above baseline to sales), 2) guaranteed burst SLA (how many GPUs can we promise within 5 mins). Ops note: eu-west capacity is constrained in Aug.
Tess Wu: From finance: we prefer committing slightly higher to avoid heavy on-demand spend. If we set safety band to 15% cost delta vs 10% is ~+$700/mo but reduces burst exposure.
Alex Patel: On the ops side, eu-west constraint matters — we should plan region routing fallback (us-east) for non-data-residency traffic. For Guppy (EU data residency), fallback limited to other EU regions; supply there is tighter — recommend 18% safety band for EU customers in Aug.
Jon Reynolds: Also reminder: prefix/KV caching + continuous batching saves ~12-18% GPU-hours for their traffic profile. If we tune batching thresholds and enable prefix cache, we can shave the reserve. Recommend we model both: conservative (18%) and optimized (12%) -> gives two pricing options.
Maria Chen: Great. Action items:
- Maria: draft capacity proposal (two options: conservative 18% EU-reserve vs optimized 12% with performance tuning) and send to sales by Fri.
- Alex: run a detailed perf sim with our latest kernels and quantization knobs, include expected token/sec and GPU-hour delta (due Thu).
- Tess: prepare pricing sheet with committed vs burst scenarios and org-level margin assumptions.
- Jon: validate warm-pool warm-up time and confirm guaranteed burst within 5/15/30 min buckets.
Anyone object to those tasks? :thumbsup:
Alex Patel: +1
Tess Wu: +1
Jon Reynolds: +1
Maria Chen: Thanks — I'll kick it off and loop in SRE for warm-pool pre-warm automation.
